newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes higher, gains trimmed late.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes higher, gains trimmed late.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher although gains were trimmed late on hedge selling and profit taking ahead of the long holiday weekend.
Floor traders said commercial and crusher buying sparked early gains along with export-related demand. They estimated overnight sales of Canadian canola to Japan at 5,000 to 8,000 tonnes.

"There was a lot of evening up ahead of the long weekend and Monday's reports," one WCE oilseed trader said. He referred to USDA's first prospective plantings report of the year and a U.S. quarterly stocks report due out early Monday.
The WCE is closed Good Friday ahead of the Easter holiday.
Gains in the CBOT soycomplex helped to fuel the advance.
May canola closed $1.90 higher at $428.90, well below the day's high of $431.00. The May WCE crush profit margin rose to -14.96 Thursday from -18.70 Wednesday.
Flaxseed was higher on commercial buying with May ending up $0.70 at $356.80. Hedge selling helped to limit gains.
Western barley futures were mostly higher aided by commission house buying. May closed up $2.00 at $144.00.
Feed wheat futures were mixed with May weakened by rolling forward of long positions into July.
May feed wheat ended off $0.30 at $171.70.
May feed peas ended $1.00 up at $215.60 with commission house buying interest noted. Oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except feed peas.)
